story:
In 2009 somebody ran a tape round this cottonwood beside the Little Lehigh Creek and read 215 inches. That is 5.46 metres of trunk, under a crown measured at 40.5 metres, about 133 feet. The Pennsylvania Big Trees register keeps both numbers and scores the tree at 378 points, which is big but not the state's biggest. It is not a champion, and nobody claims it is.

Eastern cottonwoods are the fast giants of American river bottoms. They put on wood quickly in wet ground and do not live long as great trees go, so a trunk this size speaks of a good floodplain rather than of centuries. Nobody has dated this one, and girth will not do it for a species that grows this fast.

It stands in Lehigh Parkway, a 629-acre city park that follows the Little Lehigh downstream of the Overhill Road interchange. The park is free and open every day.

Now the honest part. The register's measurement is seventeen years old and we have found no report of the tree since, and iNaturalist holds no cottonwood within 150 metres of the register's point. The register's coordinate puts it on the parkway strip by the creek without picking out one crown, so read the pin as the right few hundred metres rather than the trunk.

If you walk the creek and find a cottonwood this size, tell us it still stands, and exactly where.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its size, a cottonwood 5.46 metres round and about 40 metres tall. It stands on the Lehigh Parkway strip beside Little Lehigh Creek, downstream of the Overhill Road interchange.
name: Lehigh Parkway Eastern Cottonwood

location.address: Lehigh Parkway North, along Little Lehigh Creek downstream of the Overhill Rd interchange, Allentown, PA 18103

official_register.name: Pennsylvania Forestry Association champion tree register (PA Big Trees)

access: Free; Lehigh Parkway is a public city park of Allentown along Little Lehigh Creek, open daily
verify_notes: One source (register only), flagged. PA Big Trees record slug 'along-little-lehigh-creek-downstream-from-overhill-rd-interchange', legacy id TR20101011183717757, status approved, isPublic true, not a state or national champion, not multi-stemmed. Measured 2009: circumference 215 in (546 cm), height 133 ft (40.5 m), 378 points. Both plausible for a cottonwood on a creek floodplain. Species Eastern Cottonwood. No age in the register and no growth-rate basis taken (cottonwood is fast and short-lived, so girth does not date it). Register coordinate 40.5864776, -75.4852905 sits in the Lehigh Parkway strip beside Little Lehigh Creek; not tied to one visible crown, hence approximate. Alive NOT confirmed: the 2009 measurement is 16 years old, lifecheck says RECENT only because of an unrelated iNaturalist observation of a Callery pear 30 m away (2025-04-14), and iNaturalist shows no Populus observation within 150 m. Lehigh Parkway is 629 acres, a public park (Wikipedia). Reader should check that it still stands. Register site data (api/trees, public JSON behind pabigtrees.com) also holds nominator names and emails; none copied here. Terms of use of pabigtrees.com not found on the pages read; facts only, no photographs or text taken.
hold: Writing pass 2026-11-16, held: register only, measured 2009, and no sighting since (no Populus on iNaturalist within 150 m) for a fast, short-lived species; with an approximate pin in a 629-acre park nothing tells a visitor which cottonwood it is. Ships with a dated sighting or a GPS fix at the trunk.
